messages:
hal: CI is flaky on node18 GH runners. Local tests (vitest) pass but CI throws "SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module" on tests that import the JS SDK. Anyone seen this mismatch?

rita: Yup. Usually because package.json has "type": "module" and the runner isn't transforming the SDK package. Vitest needs the dep inlined so esbuild transpiles node_modules entrypoints.

owen: Minimal quick fix I put in our monorepo vitest config: add the SDK to deps.inline and set esbuild target. Example:```js
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    deps: { inline: ['@redwood/inference-sdk'] },
    esbuild: { target: 'es2022' }
  }
})
```
This makes CI happy.

hal: That helped, thanks. But a second issue: mocks behave differently depending on transform. `vi.mock('@redwood/inference-sdk')` sometimes can't override the default export. Tests expecting to stub SDK.default fail.

rita: We discovered the SDK build shapes the module differently for ESM vs CJS. The ESM build uses `export default new Client()` while CJS uses `module.exports = ...`. Test runners that read the package as ESM see a different module shape. Solution: ship both named and default exports in the bundles and align d.ts to expose both.

owen: Short-term workaround for tests: `import * as SDK from '@redwood/inference-sdk'` then `vi.spyOn(SDK, 'default').mockImplementation(() => ({ predict: () => Promise.resolve('x') }))`. That avoids ambiguous import semantics.

nora: Also saw `ReferenceError: self is not defined` in some unit tests that exercise edge-targeted code paths. Our runtime detection uses `typeof self !== 'undefined'` which blows up in node envs that don't define self.

hal: For test suites that need edge semantics, either set test environment to jsdom/happy-dom or add setup file polyfill: `global.self = globalThis`. Also mock `fetch` and `Headers` if code expects them.

rita: TypeScript quirks too: tests importing types from default export hit `TS2749` errors. Make sure package.json exports/types map points to correct artifacts. Example:```json
"exports":{ ".":{ "import":"./dist/esm/index.js","require":"./dist/cjs/index.js" } },
"types":"dist/types/index.d.ts"
```
And include a top-level `index.d.ts` that re-exports both named and default types.

owen: I'm going to add a tiny `index.d.ts` in the SDK that does:```ts
export type { ClientOptions } from './types'
export { Client } from './client'
export default Client
```
should smooth both runtime mocks and type imports.

hal: Good. Action items: 1) add vitest example to sdk/examples showing deps.inline + esbuild target; 2) add CONTRIBUTING note about running CI with node18/vm-modules for Jest; 3) update SDK build to export both named/default and ship updated d.ts; 4) add CI job matrix for node18 with ESM flags.

rita: I'll draft the vitest example and the CONTRIBUTING blurb. Owen can handle the d.ts and build outputs.

owen: Yep. I'll also add a small test in examples that imports the SDK both ways to catch regressions in future.

ci-bot: Reminder: when you push the PR CI will run across the matrix. Logs will include any remaining ESM import errors.

hal: Thanks team. I'll open the docs + example PR shortly. Ping me if you need pairing on the build change. :thumbsup:
